rules.adoption: Adopted 14 Oct 2026 by the profile owner under Methodology v1.1. Drafted 2026-09-25 from the four Framework 1.0 profiles (plinko 1.0.2, dice / mines / blackjack 1.0.2-draft).
rules.reproduction: Byte identity is required only for exact content. A pinned artifact's hash asserts the identity of the committed evidence — the dataset, the config, the seeds and the census (integer counts, round totals, integer-unit money) — and verify never rewrites it. A regeneration is written to outputs/run/ and compared with the committed artifact field by field: integers and strings exact; non-integer numbers within |Δ| ≤ 1e-14 + 1e-12·max(|a|,|b|), or the per-field tolerance a step declares; the diff records the runtime version and must be empty beyond tolerance. Run metadata is absent, not excluded. No verdict-bearing comparison turns on a difference below its declared tolerance. Shared with the Plinko, Dice and Mines profiles (rules.reproduction).
rules.applicability: A check applies unless its `applies` predicate over the declaration is false. The engine evaluates the predicate; a false result prints the step as n/a with the derived reason (path, declared value) and the declared value is verified against the dataset or pinned config by the rule in `declarationTruth` (conformance C-13). A declaration never asserts n/a directly; `notApplicable` lists are ignored from 1.0.2. Keno addition: a declared null means the package does not establish the fact (listed in the declaration's `unknowns`); a null never evaluates an `applies` predicate to false — the check stands. Only a measured false / 0 / null-by-design (e.g. money.balanceField) derives n/a.
rules.drawBias: R1 (carried from DICE-08 / MINES-08): each selection step exactly uniform or biased ≤ 2^-32, stated as a computed bound — rejection sampling: maxFair per range + census; float draw: floor(float32 × range) bias enumerated per range. Keno applies it to every range the without-replacement selection uses.
rules.maxPayout: R2 (carried from MINES-14 / DICE-14): every quoted multiplier lies within the declared max-odds cap; a violation is disclosed, not failed. Keno extends it to the max-payout / max-profit clip and to non-monotone paytable cells (KENO-14).
rules.phaseLabels: A package may put the elevated-stake run in the phase it labels D and have no player-seed Phase D, so KENO-06 and KENO-12 are read by purpose (client-seed variation / elevated stake), and the phase letter a package uses is recorded in the status note.

numbering: Shared with the Plinko, Dice, Mines and Blackjack profiles: KENO-nn is the same property as PLINKO-nn / DICE-nn / MINES-nn for the 24 core checks; slots 10, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 19 are game-specific; KENO-31 (scaling-edge tiers, the Keno form of PLINKO-39) and KENO-32 (auto-pick) are Keno additions.

policies.HARD_FAIL: any violation → NOT PROVABLY FAIR; verify exits 1
policies.FLAG: violation is disclosed with a limitation row; verify exits 2. A FLAG carries an origin: operator (Conditional Pass) or capture (limitation row, verdict class unchanged). Decided 2026-09-17.
policies.INFORMATIONAL: reported with its statistic and its reading, never affects the verdict and is never counted as a flag, whatever the statistic says; verify's exit code does not depend on it. The live-sample fit (check 22) is informational everywhere.
policies.RELEASE_GATE: package check that blocks publication when it fails; it never changes the verdict
policies.GRADED: not verdict-bearing; scored 1–5 in the QA scorecard and gated at release by the conformance floor

statusLegend.implemented: the check exists as specified and uses the declared parameters
statusLegend.partial: the check exists but is weaker than the profile (what is missing is stated)
statusLegend.missing: no step or package item covers it
statusLegend.n/a-declared: the casino's design makes it inapplicable; the declaration says why and the step prints it

checks.name: Seed hash integrity
checks.asserts: Every revealed server seed hashes to its published commitment under the declared encoding; the number of seeds checked equals the code constant for the audited population, not a count read from the dataset.

checks.name: Forward commitment chain
checks.asserts: For every rotation, the next-seed hash published before the rotation equals the active hash after it, and a pre-capture link anchors the chain before epoch 0. Recomputed from raw fields, never from a capture-script boolean.
checks.floor: All rotation events — zero unverified transitions
checks.declarationTruth: no key matching /next.*hash/i on any epoch record when declared null

checks.name: Hash consistency within epoch
checks.asserts: All bets sharing an epoch carry the same server-seed hash and the same client seed.

checks.name: Nonce continuity
checks.asserts: Within every epoch the nonces are exactly base … base+epochSize−1 with no gap, repeat or reorder; the base is a declared constant, not the minimum observed. An operator-side gap or repeat is a HARD FAIL; an auditor-side capture retry is a FLAG with origin = capture (limitation row, verdict class unchanged — decided 2026-09-17).
checks.floor: Nonce gap or repeat within an epoch → hard fail (methodology S1)

checks.name: Population & epoch size (G-BIND)
checks.asserts: Bets, seeds, epochs and per-phase counts equal constants in src/, every epoch has exactly epochSize bets, and the dataset's own totals are not the denominator; a secondary dataset file is pinned and counted the same way.

checks.name: Client-seed influence & Phase D recomputation
checks.asserts: A wrong client seed changes the drawn set at the rate the model predicts (0 % change → hard fail), an empty-seed control is run, every Phase D bet with a player-set seed recomputes, predictable Phase D seeds are disclosed with the exposed epochs enumerated, and the A–C generator is disclosed and is a CSPRNG.
checks.floor: Client seed not used in computation → hard fail (methodology S2); Phase D ≥ 2 distinct client seeds
checks.declarationTruth: no record labelled phase D when declared 0

checks.name: Outcome recomputation (drawn set)
checks.asserts: Every bet with a revealed seed recomputes to the recorded drawn numbers under the declared RNG and draw algorithm — as an ordered list when the capture records draw order, as a set otherwise; coverage equals expectedBets; a skipped bet is a FAIL, not an exclusion.
checks.floor: Every bet individually recomputed; a single mismatch is a hard fail

checks.name: Draw bias bound
checks.asserts: Each selection step of the draw is exactly uniform on its range or biased by no more than 2^-32, stated as a computed bound in the step detail: for rejection sampling (integer draws), maxFair per range and the rejection census; for a float draw, the floor(float32 × range) bias enumerated per range. Keno reading: every range the without-replacement selection uses (for a backward shuffle of N numbers, 2 … N; for index-into-remaining, N … N−d+1) is enumerated, not sampled.
checks.floor: Modulo bias exceeding 1/2^32 without rejection sampling → hard fail (methodology S2)

checks.name: RNG reference vectors
checks.asserts: Unit tests reproduce captured bets from their revealed seeds and fixed vectors against the operator's published algorithm or source; the adapter cites the operator source line it ports.

checks.name: Draw structure & hit counting
checks.asserts: For every bet: the drawn set has exactly numbersDrawn members, no duplicate, every member inside the declared grid and index base (a draw without replacement); the player's pick set is legal (count within picks.min … picks.max, no duplicate, inside the grid); and hits = |picks ∩ drawn| computed from the recomputed draw — never read from the operator's hit field, which is compared, not trusted. Asserted from the served record's own structure as well as from the recomputation, so a comparator that returns true unconditionally is still caught.

checks.name: Payout arithmetic
checks.asserts: payout = amount × multiplier for every paying bet and 0 for every zero-multiplier bet, compared exactly on the declared money grid or settlement rule when one exists, otherwise within an absolute tolerance no looser than 1e-8; the multiplier used is the recomputed paytable cell (KENO-13), not the served one; when the capture carries no payout field, the wallet delta is the payout and its resolution is declared.
checks.floor: Payout arithmetic error exceeding 1e-8 → hard fail (methodology S3)

checks.name: Bet-size invariance (Phase C)
checks.asserts: Every elevated-stake bet recomputes identically and pays by the same paytable cell as its base-stake config; Phase C is played on a config whose paying-cell probability gives ≥ 100 elevated-stake paying bets, so the payout path is exercised, not only the draw.
checks.floor: Phase C ≥ 100 bets at elevated stake
checks.declarationTruth: no record labelled phase C when declared 0

checks.name: Paytable provenance & served-vs-declared
checks.asserts: The served multiplier equals paytable[risk][picks][hits] of the declared, pinned paytable for every bet (exactly, or on the declared display rounding with the exact value credited), with hits taken from KENO-10; the table's origin is declared (operator config endpoint, published page, vendored source, or config + capture); every (risk, picks) row the operator served is compared cell for cell with the declared table; no operator-supplied odds or probability field is read by the derivation.

checks.name: Paytable shape & bounds
checks.asserts: Every quoted multiplier lies within the declared max-odds / max-payout cap, and the max-profit clip is declared (or declared undeclared); every non-monotone cell — a consolation payout on 0 hits, a zero between two paying cells — is enumerated and disclosed; a violation is disclosed, not failed.

checks.name: Configuration & cell coverage
checks.asserts: Phase A covers every (risk, picks) configuration with at least the floor; the payout cells reached in live play are counted and the share of theoretical RTP carried by never-reached cells is printed; coverage is asserted against the capture plan in code, not described in prose.
checks.floor: All published configurations; Phase A ≥ 50 bets per config

checks.name: Wallet / balance reconciliation
checks.asserts: When the capture carries a balance field, every consecutive-bet delta equals payout − amount exactly (or within the declared truncation resolution) or belongs to a structurally recognised deferred-credit pair; when it carries wallet credit fields instead, those settle by the same rule as the game credit; otherwise the step prints n/a — declared.
checks.declarationTruth: no running-balance-ledger key (a per-bet wallet balance before/after) on any bet record when declared null; per-bet settle amounts declared in money.walletFields are not a balance ledger and do not count

checks.name: Pick-set independence
checks.asserts: The drawn set is a function of (serverSeed, clientSeed, nonce[, cursor]) only: the declared RNG message contains no pick, risk or stake field, and this is witnessed on data — every bet recomputes with the picks excluded from the derivation, and bets that share a seed pair and differ only in their picks draw by the same function — so no player choice can steer the draw after the commitment. A draw that depends on the picks is a hard fail.

checks.name: Anti-circularity (hit probability)
checks.asserts: P(k hits | picks n) comes from the hypergeometric law alone — C(n,k)·C(N−n,d−k)/C(N,d) for grid N and d numbers drawn — checked against an exhaustive enumeration (or exact rational identity Σ_k P = 1 and the mean n·d/N) for every picks count, and never from an operator-supplied probability field; a negative control shows a corrupted probability or paytable is rejected.
checks.floor: Config probabilities diverge from independent computation → hard fail (methodology S4)

checks.name: Per-config RTP by exact enumeration vs claim
checks.asserts: For every (risk, picks) configuration, RTP = Σ_k P_hyp(k) · paytable[k] is computed in exact (rational or integer) arithmetic from the declared table and compared with the declared claim; a configuration whose derived RTP differs from the claim is a FLAG with the magnitude stated, never silently absorbed into prose; the spread across configurations is printed.

rtpClaimRule.enforcedBy: RTP_CLAIM_RULE_ENFORCED in each package's own src/rtp-claim-switch.ts, true since rule 1.2.0. The rule itself is core/rtp-claim.ts, which every package carries as a byte-identical copy (src/rtp-claim.ts); conformance C-13 compares SHA-256s and reports the package's switch value; bin/sync-rtp-claim.mjs re-vendors the rule and creates a missing switch file with false, never overwriting one.
rtpClaimRule.whileNotEnforced: the package computes the full per-setting exact RTP table, commits it (outputs/rtp-claim-table.json, SHA-256 pinned in src/rtp-settings.ts) and prints the rule's outcome as INFO; this check's own policy and every verdict are unchanged. A committed table that no longer equals the run or its pin exits 1 either way (it is evidence, not the claim).
rtpClaimRule.whenEnforced: 1.2.0: an outcome of FAIL (a setting more than the band below the stated figure, house side) is the package verdict RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5: a fail until the casino fixes the figure or the paytable, never printed as NOT PROVABLY FAIR and never a Pass, because the draws themselves pass. Verdict and exit come from rtpClaimVerdict (draw fail 1 > INCOMPLETE 3 > RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED 5 > Conditional 2 > Full 0). NO_CLAIM, NOTED and PUBLISHED are never a miss. A committed table that no longer equals the run or its pin is a reproduction failure, exit 1.
rtpClaimRule.text: The casino can publish either (1) a single number ("99% rtp") — every setting has to be within the band of it; or (2) a range ("rtp 98.65–99.07% depending on settings"), anywhere findable, fairness page or rules is fine — every setting has to sit inside it, and the range has to be the real one: bottom = their actual worst setting, top = their actual best (within the band); no "up to 99%", no range wider than reality. Our audit publishes the full per-setting table. 1.1.0: the claim is the figure shown to players, on the game page, fairness page or help page; a game with no shown figure is marked no claim (kind "none", its source naming the game page, the fairness page and the help page and saying "no RTP figure") and still gets its full per-setting table: outcome NO_CLAIM, never a FAIL, no house-side failures. 1.2.0: six places count (game page, fairness page, help page, bet panel, rules, game settings); an edge stated in the game settings counts as stated, no screenshot needed; claims may be per-setting or tiered (each stake tier held to the edge the casino states for it); a zero-edge or promotional line is noted, not tested; a casino that publishes the real per-setting figures is PUBLISHED, but a bare paytable is not.
rtpClaimRule.band: 0.1 pp (RTP_CLAIM_BAND = 0.001 as a fraction of 1). A setting within 0.1 pp of what the casino states passes; past that on the house side is a FAIL; player-favourable never fails. For a range claim the published bottom may not sit more than 0.1 pp below the true worst setting, nor the published top more than 0.1 pp above the true best.
rtpClaimRule.arithmetic: exact rationals (bigint) for every setting, the claim and the band; an RTP a package can only derive numerically (a recursive EV engine, a double convolution) enters as the exact binary value of that double, and the package states the figure's precision.
rtpClaimRule.industryContext: GLI-11 v2.0 §4.4.1(b) requires the minimum RTP to be met "at all times … at the lowest end of a non-linear paytable", naming keno spot combinations; the lab reports the minimum and maximum theoretical payout.

checks.name: Simulation Pass 1 (fresh seeds)
checks.asserts: ≥ 1,000,000 rounds per (risk, picks) configuration on pinned fresh seeds; drawn-number uniformity with the without-replacement correction, the hit histogram against the hypergeometric law, serial independence, RTP convergence; statistics re-derived in verify from the artifact's rows; the committed experiment is pinned and replayable — census byte-for-byte, derived statistics within the reproduction tolerance (rules.reproduction).

checks.name: Simulation Pass 2 (cherry-pick)
checks.asserts: Every revealed seed × 10,000 nonces; early window = the captured nonce range; the statistic is the return of the configurations the casino actually served in that epoch against the exact per-config mean and variance, with an exact or bootstrap null; every window re-derived in verify; pre-registered rule; detection power printed.

checks.name: Live-sample fit
checks.asserts: Captured drawn numbers fit the uniform grid and captured hit counts per picks count fit the hypergeometric law; informational — a few-thousand-round sample has little power and never bears the verdict.

checks.name: S5 fairness-integrity matrix
checks.asserts: exploit-testing.md carries the standardized matrix with framework IDs S5-1 … S5-8, each row Pass / Flag / Hard Fail / Not tested — disclosed, tied to a step or a capture.
checks.floor: All tests in the standardized matrix

checks.name: Player-verifier parity
checks.asserts: The site verifier's derive.js for this casino is generated from (or hash-matched to) the adapter's computeDraw; the package records that hash.
checks.declarationTruth: cite resolves; when published is false the step prints n/a and the limitations register (KENO-30) carries the row

checks.name: Player check path documented
checks.asserts: README states, in order, how a player verifies one of their own rounds: where the seed is revealed, which fields to paste, the commitment encoding, the draw algorithm, the number base (0- or 1-based), how hits are counted and which paytable cell pays — using the declaration's field names.

checks.name: Dataset & config pins
checks.asserts: The live SHA-256 of every dataset file and of the paytable/config file the derivation reads equals the constant pinned in src/; the verifier aborts on mismatch before any step runs.

checks.name: Artifacts of record
checks.asserts: Every artifact the report quotes is pinned in src/, un-ignored by name, carries no run metadata, is never rewritten by verify (verify writes only to outputs/run/), and every numeric leaf has a declared value domain; the pin asserts the identity of the committed evidence, and byte identity across machines is required only for exact content — dataset, config, seeds, census — while derived statistics are compared at the reproduction tolerance, never by bytes (rules.reproduction).

checks.name: Fresh-clone reproduction
checks.asserts: On a fresh clone, npm ci && npm test prints N/N with the Full Pass verdict and exit 0 within the budget, without modifying any pinned artifact; a regeneration (test:full) is written to outputs/run/ and compared with the committed artifacts field by field — integers and strings exact, non-integer numbers within |Δ| ≤ 1e-14 + 1e-12·max(|a|,|b|) or the per-field tolerance a step declares — with the diff and the runtime version recorded in outputs/run/diff.json and nothing beyond tolerance; step counts in README/MANIFEST equal the suite; the audit ID is assigned; the runtime is pinned.

checks.name: Mutation battery
checks.asserts: A step-named mutation registry runs in a disposable copy; every scored step has at least one mutation that kills it; declared survivors are tied to limitation IDs; forged-evidence batteries are included.

checks.name: Disclosure register & evidence appendix
checks.asserts: MANIFEST carries the declared-limitations register with closure evidence, the load-bearing premises marked ASSUMED where unwitnessed, and evidence.md numbers every exhibit from E01 with its evidential role; no internal QA material ships in the package.

checks.name: Scaling-edge / bet-size tier audit
checks.asserts: When the operator serves a bet-size tier ladder (scaling edge): every bet is priced by the tier its stake falls in — its paytable is that tier's table and its served edge equals the tier's edge; the tiers are contiguous with no gap or overlap; every tier's paytable reproduces its stated edge by exact enumeration (KENO-19 per tier); and the capture exercises at least one bet above the first tier boundary. When the declaration says no ladder at capture, the pinned config is read to confirm it (declarationTruth) and every bet's served edge equals the flat edge. A ladder that appears after the capture is a re-certification item recorded in the register, never read into the captured population.
checks.declarationTruth: the pinned operator config carries an empty or absent scaling-edge ladder, and every bet's served edge field equals the flat edge, when declared false

checks.name: Auto-pick vs manual pick
checks.asserts: When the operator offers an auto-pick (random pick) control: the capture records which bets used it, auto-picked sets are legal pick sets (KENO-10) that enter the settlement exactly as manual picks do (same paytable cell, same draw function — KENO-17), and where the auto-pick is generated (client or server, seeded or not) is declared; auto-pick outcomes are not favoured or disfavoured relative to manual picks at the same config. When offered but not captured, the gap is disclosed, not passed.
checks.declarationTruth: no auto-pick / random-pick control on the operator's Keno page or in its bet request shape when declared false; a declared null is unknown and never derives n/a
